edit.description: The guard suite's last two hand-spelled lock rows. `post_edge_harness` (:865) writes the fixture lock through `common::GuardLock` (tests/it/common/mod.rs:459), and two cases then read that lock back off disk and `format!` a raw `[[declaration.clause]]` block onto its bytes — `the_post_edge_stays_silent_where_no_locus_declared_clause_binds` (:807, a `root.fresh` row) and `the_post_edge_stays_silent_where_no_fresh_clause_binds` (:831, a `root.reachable` row). Both spell label/predicate/severity, which is exactly what `GuardLock::clause_row` (common/mod.rs:518) types and `clause_table` (:674) renders, so the fold is: give `post_edge_harness` the clause its two callers need (its other four call sites — :640, :679, :704, :766 — declare none), declare the row there, and delete the text append. What the append costs is the read-back: text concatenated after `GuardLock::write` (:540) never passes that method's `parse_declarations` assertion, and `family()` (src/drift.rs:4636) answers an empty vec for an absent family key, so a renamed clause family or optional column in `src/` leaves both cases green over a lock that binds no clause — and both assert an absence (empty guard output), the vacuity class `specs/process/engineering.md`, "A green verdict is proven non-vacuous" names. Out of scope and untouched: the requirement-row lock at :263 (a `check`-argument fixture declaring no mode, which this home's mode-first constructor cannot yet spell) and the deliberately-unparseable lock at :918.

summary: Two guard post-edge cases append a raw clause row onto the lock the shared home just wrote, so the row skips the read-back that keeps the spelling honest.

tests.asserts: both post-edge unbound-clause cases stay green with their clause declared through the shared home, so GuardLock::write's read-back covers the row; renaming the clause family or its `severity` column in src/ turns them red instead of leaving them silent

acceptance: `cargo test` green, no `[[declaration.` text left in tests/it/cli.rs's two post-edge clause cases, and both cases red under a renamed clause family in `src/`.
notes: Residue of GUARD-LOCK-FIXTURES-FOLD-INTO-ONE-HOME (890db08a), which folded 22 hand-spelled guard locks into `common::GuardLock` and left these two appends behind because `post_edge_harness` owns the write. The wider hand-spelled-lock class in acceptance.rs, session_start.rs, check_cost.rs, hook_kind.rs and coverage_note.rs is not this entry's; SESSION-START-LOCK-FIXTURES-FOLD-INTO-ONE-HOME takes the next slice. scoped at 2f95f0a1
